alex: Heads-up: running a perf sweep on Mistral 8x7B sliding-window workloads and hit a consistent p95 spike when sequences cross 4096->4100. Looks like KV offsets are drifting at window boundaries.
anya: repro steps? which model binary + max_pos? :thinking:
alex: model tag mistral-8x7b-v1.2, reported max_position_embeddings=8192 but runtime treats some shards as 4096. Repro: generate with seq_len distribution 2-6k, steady QPS 120, batching disabled. p50 ~40ms fine, p95 jumps from 120ms -> 340ms when a request lands at window boundary.
kevin: can you paste the kernel-selector log around the event? might be switching kernels mid-stream.
alex: pasted below (snip):
```
[2026-03-15T14:03:21Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=optimized_matmul_v2 seq_len=4100 heads=32 kv_dim=64 fallback=generic_gemm
[2026-03-15T14:03:21Z] kv_cache: allocate shard0 offset=4096 shard_len=4096
[2026-03-15T14:03:21Z] kernel_switch: reason=seq_len_bound_crossed old=optimized_matmul_v2 new=generic_gemm
[2026-03-15T14:03:21Z] perf: token_throughput_drop 2.8x
```
kevin: aha — selector flips because it sees effective seq_len>kernel_threshold. But the KV allocation used shard offsets based on previous window size (4096), so there's an off-by-one alignment when backend falls back. That explains the extra memcpy/slow path.
sasha: do we have profiler flame for the slow case? is memcpy dominating?
alex: yes, memcpy + recompile-ish path. NVTX shows a big stall inside `kv_cache->remap()` and then generic_gemm kernel has poor occupancy for this shape.
anya: sounds like two issues: 1) kernel cutoff threshold too coarse for 8x7b's head/kv dims, 2) allocator assumes fixed window boundary (4096) while some shards advertise 8192. Need to reconcile model metadata vs shard metadata.
kevin: quick experiments: lowering kernel_selector threshold from 4096 to 3840 keeps optimized_matmul_v2 for 4k-ish requests and avoids fallback for our typical shapes. Also adding a cheap check: if current_kv_offset != expected_offset -> force-kernel-stay for this request to avoid realloc. Results: p95 drops ~2.6x in local sim.
anya: risky to force kernel stay globally. Could we instead make allocator lazy-resize: allow offset mismatch but keep logical view contiguous (i.e., allocate bigger backing buffer once per-shard and avoid rebind during request)?
sasha: that's safer. Also update the kernel selector to consider kv_dim/head_count shape heuristics not just seq_len threshold. For 8x7b the matmul tiling favors head_count=32 and kv_dim=64 — we should bias to optimized kernel for those combos up to ~4600.
runtime-bot: deploy status: canary build rtd-2026-03-15-kernel-fix queued for eng-runtime/canary (no SLA impact).
alex: here's a proposed patch (pseudo):
```
// kernel_selector.cpp
if (shape.matches(heads=32, kv_dim=64) && seq_len <= 4600) {
  prefer_kernel = optimized_matmul_v2;
} else if (seq_len <= kernel_threshold) {
  prefer_kernel = optimized_matmul_v2;
} else {
  prefer_kernel = generic_gemm;
}

// kv_allocator.cpp
// lazy-resize: if requested_offset > allocated_len -> allocate new backing only during warmup, mark request to use old backing until done
```
kevin: +1 to both. Also add unit test: simulate sliding window where multiple concurrent requests straddle a boundary and ensure no realloc during active generation.
anya: can we add telemetry tags: `kernel_switch_reason` and `kv_realloc=true/false` so we can filter incidents?
sasha: yes, add event for `kv_offset_mismatch` with sample stack and sequence_bucket.
alex: after local patch, microbench numbers: before p95=340ms, p50=38ms, tokens/sec=220. After: p95=105ms, p50=36ms, tokens/sec=540. Memory overhead +6% for lazy backing but steady CPU/GPU utilization improved.
kevin: please open a short PR with changelog & perf numbers, and add an opt-in runtime flag `--aggressive-kernel-bias` so Dedicated customers can opt-in in case it affects quality.
anya: also schedule a short canary in us-west-2 with traffic ramp to catch cross-region shard metadata misreporting.
sasha: note: this may interact with RoPE scaling — if rope_scale != 1.0 the effective kv cache usage pattern differs, we should run quick pass on models with rope scaling (mixtral variants).
alex: logged followups: PR #, canary job id, and add eval prompts to verify identical completions before/after for quality regressions.
kevin: thanks — great catch.
anya: thanks all :thumbsup:
